instruction: Set the Snake game speed to 20 frames per second in the settings file.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent opened VS Code with Snake game project, browsed all 4 files (food.py, main.py, settings.py, snake.py), correctly identified the code structure, attempted Find & Replace to fix collision detection, then tried adding a @property to snake.py but introduced IndentationError. Ran python3 main.py, got IndentationError. Spent remaining 50 turns debugging indentation without resolving.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate VS Code file explorer, open files, read and understand Python code, open terminal, run shell commands, install packages via pip, use Find & Replace dialog
metadata.failure_analysis: Model correctly identified the bug direction but struggled with precise text editing in VS Code. Added a @property but broke indentation. Could not recover from the IndentationError despite multiple attempts.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to changing a single numeric constant (FPS) in settings.py. The model demonstrated it can open settings.py and understand its contents. Changing 10 to 20 is a minimal edit within model's capability.
metadata.explanation: Task requires changing FPS from 10 to 20 in settings.py. Getter runs python3 to extract FPS value. Metric checks if FPS equals 20.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly extracts FPS value by executing settings.py as Python and printing the FPS variable - directly reads the state the instruction targets
Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule': accesses expected.get('expected_fps', 20) directly from the rules dict
Expected value (20) matches the instruction requirement exactly
Postconfig sends Ctrl+S to save the file before evaluation, ensuring the getter reads the latest state from disk
Complete coverage: the single instruction requirement (FPS = 20) is fully verified by the evaluator
Error handling is sound: getter catches exceptions and returns error dict, metric returns 0.0 for error results
